The ambiguity 'Mainnet activation is described as 'shortly (a few days or weeks) after' Pectra activation without a precise timeline.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The assumption 'Alternate data sources (e2store, Portal Network, EIP-7801) will be available and reliable when clients need to retrieve pre-merge data.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'Data retrieved from alternate sources can be trusted to be authentic if it validates against known block hashes.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'All consensus layer clients will have implemented EIP-6110 before history expiry, eliminating CL dependency on EL deposit logs.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'Applications and tooling will be updated to handle data unavailability gracefully or use alternate sources.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
After history expiry activation, clients must return appropriate error responses for unavailable historical data rather than incorrect data.
Data retrieved from alternate sources (e2store, Portal Network) must be validated against known block hashes before being served.
History expiry must not affect the ability to validate new blocks on the canonical chain.

The ambiguity 'The proposal states gas is charged 'only for memory that is actually written to' but the formula charges for output_start + min(output_size, n), which may include unwritten bytes if output_start > current MSIZE.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The behavior when output_start + output_size overflows 2^256-1 is not explicitly specified.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The assumption 'The calling contract trusts that the output bounds enforcement prevents the called contract from corrupting memory outside the designated output area.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'Contracts using output_size = 2^256-1 for dynamic sizing must be prepared to handle the gas cost of any return data size.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'Objects stored in memory after CALL operations must be relocatable since absolute positions may change based on actual return data size.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
After a CALL with output bounds, the caller's memory beyond output_start + output_size must remain unmodified.
The output_start and output_size parameters must not cause integer overflow when computing memory expansion gas.
Memory gas charging must be consistent whether memory is written by CALL output or by direct MSTORE operations.

The ambiguity 'The specification states 'permanently set the code' but also allows clearing delegation with address 0x0, making 'permanent' misleading.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'Transaction pool recommendation to 'not accept more than one pending transaction' for delegated EOAs is not formally specified.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'No specification for how delegation indicator interacts with CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes if executed in delegated context.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The phrase 'delegation loops only follow first level' does not clearly define behavior for chains A->B->C where B also has delegation.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'Users signing authorization tuples understand they are granting code execution rights to their account.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'Attackers can observe pending transactions and attempt front-running or sandwich attacks on delegation setup.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Existing contracts relying on msg.sender == tx.origin for EOA detection will have that invariant broken.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Delegation target contracts will properly implement nonce/replay protection within their own logic.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The 0xef0100 prefix is reserved and will not conflict with future EVM features or EOF.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Wallet and dApp developers will update UIs to properly display and warn about authorization signing.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
Authorization tuples in EIP-7702 transactions must contain valid ECDSA signatures from the delegating EOA.
An EOA with delegation code set (0xef0100 prefix) must resolve delegation only one level deep—no transitive delegation chains.
After a delegation is cleared (address set to 0x0...0), the account must behave as a standard EOA with no code.
The nonce of a delegating EOA must be incremented atomically with the delegation setup to prevent replay.
The chain_id in the authorization tuple must match the current chain or be 0 (wildcard) for cross-chain authorization.
Existing contracts using tx.origin == msg.sender checks must be aware that EIP-7702 delegated EOAs break this invariant.

The ambiguity 'The boundaries between layers are not precisely defined, particularly for EIPs that span multiple layers.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'No explicit process is defined for handling EIPs that affect multiple layers simultaneously.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'All client implementations will adopt consensus layer changes uniformly.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'EIP authors correctly identify the layer their proposal affects.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
Each EIP must be classified into exactly one layer as defined in the EIP-4 classification system.

The ambiguity 'The statement 'disconnect immediately' does not specify which disconnect reason code should be used.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'Peers honestly report their forkid in the Status message.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'All nodes have accurate knowledge of past and upcoming fork block numbers.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The forkid mechanism provides sufficient protection against connecting to nodes on incompatible forks.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
A node must verify the peer's forkid during the eth/64 handshake and disconnect immediately if incompatible.
The forkid computation must include all past and known future fork block numbers in chronological order.
After a successful eth/64 handshake, both peers must be on compatible fork configurations.

The ambiguity 'The EIP does not specify behavior for nodes that have not upgraded when the fork activates.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The ambiguity 'Block >= 0 on future testnets is vague about which testnets this applies to.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'A sufficient majority of network nodes will upgrade before the activation block.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The activation block number was chosen to give adequate time for coordination and upgrades.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
Nodes must have upgraded to Homestead-compatible software before block 1,150,000 on mainnet.
After the Homestead activation block, all Homestead consensus rules must be enforced for every subsequent block.

The ambiguity 'The behavior when immediate operand is beyond code boundary is not explicitly stated' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The ambiguity 'The exact definition of 'exceptional failure' is referenced but not defined' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'The EVM stack implementation supports efficient indexed access to deep stack positions' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Static analysis tools can still accurately track stack state with extended depth operations' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Compilers generating code with these opcodes correctly compute stack indices' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The immediate operand for extended stack access opcodes must reference a valid stack position (within current stack depth).
After executing a DUP or SWAP with extended depth, the stack size must change by exactly the expected amount (+1 for DUP, 0 for SWAP).
Extended stack access opcodes must trigger exceptional failure if the operand references beyond the current stack depth.

The ambiguity 'The standard 'does not include replay protection' - applications must implement their own, but no standard mechanism is defined.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The specification states domain separator fields 'must appear in order' but also says 'user-agents should accept any order'. This is contradictory.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The phrase 'Protocol designers only need to include the fields that make sense for their signing domain' leaves significant discretion without guidance.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'Handling of recursive struct types with circular references is not explicitly addressed.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The assumption 'Wallets will faithfully display the typed data to users before signing, without modification or obfuscation.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'Attackers cannot construct a different typed data structure that produces the same hash as a legitimate message.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The chainId in the domain separator matches the actual chain where the signature will be verified.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Verifying contracts correctly implement the EIP-712 encoding and hashing algorithm.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The dApp correctly encodes the typed data structure according to its intended meaning.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
Two structurally different typed data messages must never produce the same EIP-712 hash (collision resistance).
The domain separator must include the correct chainId matching the chain where the signature will be verified.
Wallets must display the full typed data structure to users before signing—no fields may be hidden or obfuscated.
Recursive struct types must be detected and rejected or handled to prevent infinite encoding loops.
After EIP-712 hash computation, the result must be deterministic—same inputs always produce the same hash.

The ambiguity 'The specification does not clearly define the ordering of pending deposit entries when multiple validators are migrated simultaneously during the upgrade.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The term 'compounding withdrawal credentials' is referenced without a full definition of which credential prefixes qualify.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The assumption 'All nodes in the network will reach ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH at approximately the same time and apply the upgrade atomically.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'The validator set state is consistent and complete at the fork boundary, with no partially-applied state transitions.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'The exit churn limits computed during fork upgrade are sufficient to prevent mass exit attacks in the first Electra epoch.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
During the Electra fork transition, pending deposit entries must preserve their original ordering from the deposit queue.
After Electra fork upgrade, validators with compounding withdrawal credentials must have their balances correctly migrated.
Exit churn limits computed during fork transition must prevent more than the allowed number of validators from exiting per epoch.

The ambiguity 'The definition of 'touched' includes 'zero-value transfers' but does not clarify if failed calls also count as touches.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The phrase 'No account may change state from non-existent to existent-but-empty' does not specify enforcement mechanism.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The ambiguity 'Interaction between nonce increment and revert is not explicitly specified.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'All client implementations track touched accounts consistently during transaction execution.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The state trie can efficiently handle account deletion operations at transaction end.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Miner rewards and SUICIDE operations are correctly identified as account touches.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
After transaction execution, all empty accounts that were touched during the transaction must be removed from state.
No account may transition from non-existent to existent-but-empty (zero nonce, zero balance, no code).
The state tracking mechanism must record all accounts touched during transaction execution, including zero-value transfers.
Account deletion via EIP-161 must be applied atomically at the end of transaction execution, not during intermediate steps.
